newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Dengue fever hits flood-stricken south Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Dengue fever hits flood-stricken south Vietnam.

text.p: A dengue fever outbreak in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta is adding to problems for some four million people already hit by the region's worst floods in years, relief workers said on Monday.
An official at the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies told Reuters that 4,000 cases of the mosquito-borne disease had been reported so far. Nine people have died.
"There seems to be a high (sea) tide at present so the flood waters cannot flow out so easily," said the IFRC's Leif Tybell. "This is causing a problem as the water is becoming stagnant."
This year's flooding, in Vietnam's main food-producing region, is the worst in more than two decades.
Eight provinces have been directly affected. Separate flash floods have also caused damage in surrounding areas.
Damage has been put at more than $100 million.
Flooding in the Mekong Delta has become an an annual problem. But despite preparations about 120 people, more than 100 of them children, have died in recent weeks.
Tybell added that the impact of the floods was hardest on the poor, who have been hit by serious floods for three consecutive years.

"We're not talking about famine or disaster, but it is affecting the poor and making their lives really hard," he said. "There's a risk they will never be able to get out from this destructive cycle."
Dengue fever resembles malaria, but is rarely fatal. Victims usually complain of headaches, fever and pains in the joints.
Vietnam said on Monday that government ministries had been instructed to help the victims.
